title: Drop Repeated Values From a Sorted Chain
statement:
You get the head of a linked list sorted in non-decreasing order. Remove every node whose value appears more than once, including the first copy, so only values that occur exactly once remain. Return the head of the resulting list, still sorted.

Lists are written as arrays, like [1, 2, 2, 3]; the empty list is [].

examples.why: 2 and 4 occur more than once, so all their copies go. Keeping one 2 and one 4 would be the easier "dedupe" problem, not this one.
The head itself is removed, so the returned head is a different node.
Every value repeats, so nothing is left.

constraints: The list is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Since the list is sorted, all copies of a value sit next to each other. How do you tell that the node you are on starts a run of copies?
Removing the head is awkward when you hold a pointer to it. Put a dummy node in front of the list.
Keep prev, the last node you are sure to keep. If the node after it starts a run of two or more equal values, skip the whole run by linking prev past it; otherwise move prev forward.

explain.intuition:
Sorting puts all copies of a value in one run, so the question for each run is just "is it longer than one node?". Walk the list run by run. A run of length one is kept; a longer run is cut out entirely by linking the node before it to the node after it.

Cutting needs the node before the run, and the very first run may need cutting too. A dummy node in front of the head gives every run a predecessor, so there is no special case, and the answer is simply dummy.next.
steps: Create dummy with dummy.next = head and set prev = dummy.
If cur.next has the same value, advance cur to the last node of the run and set prev.next = cur.next; do not move prev.
Otherwise the value is unique: set prev = cur.
pitfalls: Keeping one copy of each repeated value. Here all copies must go.
Moving prev forward after cutting a run. The next run might also need cutting, as in [1, 1, 2, 2], and prev must still sit before it.
Returning the original head, which may have been removed.

solutions.title: Count values, then rebuild
solutions.idea: Count every value, then build a new list from the values whose count is exactly one.

solutions.title: Dummy node and run skipping
solutions.idea: Keep a pointer to the last node that stays. Cut out each run longer than one by relinking past it.

followups: The list is not sorted. How do you remove every value that appears more than once?
Keep values that appear at most twice instead of exactly once.
